translation:
For now, I'm gonna go cheer myself up by
complaining to the computer society!

I won't be satisfied until I've given them a
piece of my mind!

So said a wide-eyed Haruhi as she leapt off
towards the clubroom building.
Hey, waaait, I'm coming toooo!
Good grief…

Miraculously, Haruhi has left. Looks like I can
relax for the time being.
Umm… It looks like everyone had a rough time.
Indeed, it was quite the struggle.

Koizumi, what did you even do that classifies
as a "struggle”?

At least I didn't see you do anything
particularly helpful.

I was able to use my abilities in that space,
although to a limited capacity.

I was blocking off anything from the
alternate space that might interfere with you.
You were…? I totally didn't notice.

I wonder, could there have been blades of
light flying towards me…

…like that time before, when I was attacked
by a classmate?
I'll just give you my thanks for now.

If we're offering thanks, then to the others
as well. Everyone put in a distinguished effort.

He's absolutely right. If it weren't for
everyone here, who knows what we'd have done.

Asahina and Nagato, thank you for doing
such a fine job.
No, not at all. Compared to everyone else…
All I did was talk with Suzumiya.

No, that's exactly what I mean—I can't
imagine how hard it must've been.

But I suppose that's just another aspect of
Asahina's charm.

Well then, shall we go pay a visit to the
computer society as well?
I guess so.

Oh, right. The tea should be getting cold by
now, right? I can brew some more.

Asahina said so with a smile on her face.
Nothing like tea after hard work, right?
Wait.
…What's wrong, Nagato?
We have not yet dealt with the source.

Nagato was holding the laptop we got from
inside the classroom.

So that thing is the main body of a data
lifeform after all?
No.
Huh…

In this device is one part of a data lifeform
with limited functionality.

Th-then the main body is still out there
somewhere?!
Nagato gave a simple nod.

We thought we'd defeated the final boss, but
it turns out it was only a miniboss—

It seems we've been faced with an RPG trope
so overplayed it's tiresome.

It appears to be in our best interest to deal
with it in haste. Let's start immediately.
I'll go keep Suzumiya company.
There is no need. The main body is here.

Nagato held out her other hand, within which
was a thin slab the size of a postage stamp.
Is that a memory card?

Yes. A possession of the Computer Research
Society president.
As she spoke, Nagato pointed directly at me.
Wha…
Kyon is…?
Wait wait wait! It's me?!
No. The main body is there.
There…? Oh.

Upon further inspection, Nagato was pointing
at my chest pocket.
If I remember correctly, there should be a…
This is… the president's memory card?

Pinching the memory card between my fingers,
I held it up to my eyes.

It goes without saying, but it looked very
much like a normal memory card.

The main body of the data lifeform sleeps
within.
What do you mean, "sleeps”?

Its functions are partitioned, and it has
self-compressed and suspended.

Compressed and suspended… In other words,
it wasn't active as a lifeform.

So that's why even Nagato couldn't find it at
first.
Yes.

So then, what are the functions you said it
partitioned?
The ability to create potential space.
So it's as I thought…

I guess that's what the mysterious space
was?

All it did was generate that nuisance of a
room, so what was it trying to accomplish?

The data lifeform needed more information for
its evolution process.

In order to support that, it transferred to a
device with a greater storage capacity.

But a laptop has more storage than a memory
card, right?

By invading a device that can more easily
transmit, it has more chances to propagate.

I suppose reaching a desktop computer would
certainly be more comfortable than a laptop.
It's just like a virus, don't you think?

If it gained the ability to connect to the
internet and perpetuate its evolution…

…It probably could have been able to spread
throughout the entire world.
W-what?! Th-that would've been a disaster!

For sure. If we had left it alone, it would've
eventually made its way to Haruhi.

If that happened, the world would've truly
found itself in a crisis.
Wh-what should we do now?

For the time being, we should do something
about this memory card, right?
Yes.

In order to delete its contents digitally, we'd
need to temporarily connect it to a computer.
But, if it's a virus, won't it infect the—
Physical deletion will suffice.

So you're saying we can just bend it with
pliers or burn it in an incinerator?

If we don't wish for Miss Suzumiya to notice,
we'll need to wait for another opportunity.

You really want me to just carry around
something this dangerous?

We need to destroy it ASAP, don't you think?
Put an end to Haruhi's curiosity.

Otherwise, she'll say she wants to know the
contents and bring it to the computer society.
Here.
R-right.
I placed the memory card in Nagato's palm.
And just like that, it crumbled away into dust.

The memory card had been completely
destroyed within the palm of Nagato's hand.

That belonged to the computer society
president, right?
Yes, but we had no other choice.

Would it help to offer the president my
condolences?
Well, that's finally all sorted out.

There shouldn't be any more strange girls
appearing…

…or classroom entrapments for that matter,
right?
Um, excuse me…
…Is there something more?
What's this mop doing here?

If you're done using it, you should put it
away, you know?
Ah, it's probably best you don't touch that.
Huh? Is there something special about it?

Indeed there is. It's a special mop made by
Miss Nagato for use in alternate space.

Its attributes were appended to affect wave
functions, lowering existence probability.
Wha—?!

Th-that's dangerous! That's really
dangerous, isn't it?!

Without question. We should've disposed of it
right away.
I used such a dangerous thing…?

Well, I don't really get the theory behind it
anyway.

I see. Well, a practical way to explain it would
be through Schrödinger's cat.
What the hell is that?

Say that you have a box containing a cat,
radium, and a poisonous gas.

The gas will only release in response to alpha
particles, which may be emitted by the radium.

The emission of said particles only occurs
occasionally, however.

So then—after some time passes, you open
the lid of the box. Is the cat dead or alive?

If any of those particles have been emitted
then it's dead, otherwise it's alive, right?

Only the outcome is important here. Is it dead
or alive?
It could be either dead or alive, I guess.
Exactly. That's what a wave function is.

Until we observe, the outcome is unknown. It's
in a state where either case is possible.

We can assume the chance to be fifty-fifty.
But what if it leaned further in one direction?

Let's say we increased the probability of a
favorable outcome.

Or perhaps, made an unfavorable outcome
less likely.
Is that even possible?

It would seem so. In this case, the chance of
alternate space existing was increased.

But likewise, Miss Nagato's enhanced mop
reduced that possibility.

In fact, there's a person very close to us
who is unconsciously capable of such feats.
Haruhi, huh?

That's right. As long as she wishes for the
cat to live…

…It wouldn't matter how long you leave it in
the box, the cat would still be alive, right?
On the contrary…
On the contrary?

It would probably have turned into something
other than a cat—maybe even grown wings.

Her head's filled with fantasies. She should
really become a magician or something.

Sufficiently advanced technology is
indistinguishable from magic.

Miss Asahina, is the technique for your time
travel science or magic?

Umm… it's probably <classified information>, but
it's not anything like magic.
…It's exactly as Nagato said.

Then what about you, Nagato? Science, or
magic?
Hmm…

Humans label hidden knowledge and things
they don't understand…
…as occult.

When you say occult… you mean ghost stories
and urban legends?

People react to things they don't understand
with fear and apprehension. That's why.

It certainly seems that way. Even the mop
that just rolled in front of me is an unknown.

I don't know if it's the pinnacle of scientific
theory, or if it houses some magical energy.
So what is it, then?

Anything wiped by this mop sees a reduction in
the probability of its existence.

It can perhaps—no, it truly does stop things
from coming into existence.
Isn't that right, Miss Nagato?
Yes.
So it's a magic mop that can erase anything?

For a mop, this really seems to be something
quite terrifying.

It's nothing like that homing mode baseball
bat—this is some next-level insanity.

Nagato, please, could you hurry up and get
rid of this disturbing thing?
Understood.

Good grief. Well, I guess everything's finally
settled.
About Haruhi
